Divides a raster into the basins of its minima, or of its maxima if inverted, as the crowns of the trees of a canopy height model, with the immersion algorithm of Vincent and Soille (1991).

**Toolbox folder:** Lesto › vegetation<br>
**Status:** Experimental<br>
**Keywords:** watershed, segmentation, crowns, lidar<br>
**Authors:** Christopher Mei, Lee Vincent and Pierre Soille 1991, Andrea Antonello (hm port)<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.lesto.modules.vegetation.WatershedAlgorithm`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inRaster` | raster file |  |  | The raster to divide, as a canopy height model. |
| `doInvert` | boolean |  | `false` | If true, the raster is flooded upside down, from its maxima: the basins are then the crowns around the tops of a canopy height model. |
| `doBorders` | boolean |  | `true` | If true, the output has 1 on the watershed lines between the basins, else the number of the basin of each cell. |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outRaster` | output file |  | The watershed lines or the basins. |

**References**

- Vincent, L., Soille, P. (1991). Watersheds in digital spaces: an efficient algorithm based on immersion simulations. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 13(6), 583-598.
